article.headline: UK Prime Minister Condemns Lenient Sentences for Teenage Rapists
article.summary: Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer has expressed outrage over the lenient sentences given to three teenage boys who raped two teenage girls in separate incidents in Hampshire. The boys, who were 13 and 14 years old at the time of the crimes, were spared custodial sentences and instead given Youth Rehabilitation Orders. The prime minister has described the case as "appalling" and said it is right that the attorney general is reviewing the sentences.
article.body:
The case has sparked widespread condemnation, with many expressing shock and outrage at the lenient sentences handed down to the teenage rapists. The two victims, who were 14 and 15 years old at the time of the attacks, were raped in separate incidents in Fordingbridge, Hampshire, in November 2024 and January 2025. The boys, who are now aged 14 and 15, filmed the rapes on their phones and shared some of the footage online.

The sentencing hearing was held at Southampton Crown Court, where Judge Nicholas Rowland said he wanted to "avoid criminalising these children unnecessarily." However, the decision has been widely criticized, with many arguing that the sentences are too lenient. One of the victims, who is now 16, told the BBC that the decision was like a "rock straight in my face" and made her feel like the justice system had failed her.

The prime minister has described the girl's testimony as "harrowing and brave" and said that the girls at the heart of the case have shown "extraordinary bravery and strength in heinous circumstances." He added that it is right that the attorney general is reviewing the sentences and that he expects the decision to be made urgently. The attorney general has 28 days to decide whether to refer the sentences to the Court of Appeal.

The case has also sparked a wider debate about the justice system and how it handles cases of rape and sexual assault. Many have argued that the sentences are too lenient and do not reflect the severity of the crimes. The government has said that it shares the public's shock at the details of the case and that its thoughts are with the young victims during this distressing time.

The review of the sentences is expected to be conducted swiftly, with Cabinet Minister Darren Jones saying that he expects the decision to be made quicker than the 28-day timeframe. The case has also sparked a reaction from other politicians, with Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch saying that she is "sickened" by the case and that the punishment was "no punishment at all."
article.takeaway: The UK prime minister has condemned the lenient sentences given to three teenage boys who raped two teenage girls, describing the case as "appalling" and saying that it is right that the attorney general is reviewing the sentences.
